analysis.title: US midterm elections: 3 scenarios for markets
key_insights: US midterms are on 3 November, with all 435 House seats and 35 of 100 Senate seats up. Polls show Democrats leading nationally by around eight percentage points, and Trump's approval rating is at new lows.
Cost-of-living worries tied to motor fuel prices and the war with Iran, plus AI job-security concerns, are cited as key drivers of voter sentiment. Support for the Iran conflict has wavered.
Pollsters and prediction markets anticipate a Democrat takeover of Congress, but ING notes surprises do happen. A Democratic win would constrain Trump and shift his focus to foreign and trade policy.

Scenario 1 (Republican hold of both chambers) is seen as least likely. It would bring more border enforcement, tariffs used to push partners to align with US policy, more defence spending, deregulation and an aggressive stance on Iran.

Under Scenario 1, bond yields rise along the whole curve: the 10yr likely moves above 5.5% and stays there, and the 2yr rises to around 5%. The dollar would be cyclically strongest (looser fiscal, tighter monetary policy). Emerging market currencies and possibly the euro (via French government bonds) come under pressure.

Scenario 2 (Democrat House, Republican Senate) is described as broadly in line with the central market discount. Legislative gridlock follows, so Trump relies on executive powers, mainly foreign policy, trade and defence. Iran and tariffs are likely to be the focus.

Under Scenario 2, front-end yields ease lower while back-end yields keep an upside bias within ING's preferred 5.25% to 5.5% range. The dollar largely prices this in, with a Fed intent on at least one more rate hike.

The debt ceiling is likely to become an issue by mid-summer 2027 with little room for compromise. This risks an extended government shutdown, potentially longer than last October's, which reduced 4Q 2025 GDP growth by a full percentage point. A prolonged shutdown could weigh on the dollar in 2H 2027.

Scenario 3 (Democrat clean sweep) is the most likely outcome in prediction markets, though analysts remain split between it and Scenario 2. Democrats would push back harder on Iran, Israel support and tariff escalation.

Under Scenario 3, front-end yields come under upside pressure. The 10yr risks getting toward 5.5% without breaking above it, as tariffs act as a tax hike but inflation also pressures yields. The dollar could see a little weakness.
Democrats would use House control to stall data centre construction in their districts and increase scrutiny of tech companies and AI development. Fossil fuel producers may face similar challenges.

For Europe, a Republican hold raises pressure on Europe and the risk of a forced Russia-Ukraine deal. A split Congress with a trade-focused Trump raises global volatility and the risk of an economic accident with Europe. A Democrat sweep could lead some European countries to slow defence spending increases.

China's main response will be wait-and-see under any outcome. The US-China trade truce expires in January. A constrained Trump focused on foreign and trade policy could put China back in the crosshairs.

sector_views.rationale: A Democratic House would increase scrutiny of tech companies and AI development, with congressional hearings and efforts to stall data centre construction. Under a Republican hold, AI innovation would be fast-tracked.

Fossil fuel producers may face challenges under Democratic control, while a Republican hold would incentivise fossil and nuclear energy production. Escalation in the Middle East could push energy prices higher.

macro_indicators.reading: at least one more rate hike

risk_factors: Polls could be wrong and surprises happen in US elections.
Fiscal sustainability fears intensify under a Republican hold, especially if Trump pushes through "Trump dividend" payments that force the Fed to respond with higher rates.
Debt ceiling standoff by mid-summer 2027 risks an extended government shutdown and a data blackout for the Fed.
Escalation of military action in the Middle East could disrupt energy markets and lift prices.
Impeachment proceedings or investigations of cabinet members could toxify the US political situation.
US-China trade truce expiry in January could revive a high-tariff scenario.
A constrained Trump may accept more political or market disruption in pursuit of foreign and trade policy objectives.
vol_and_positioning: A bad pain trade in Treasuries may be needed before a Republican-controlled Congress acts on the fiscal deficit, which would then pull yields back down.
Higher bond yields would continue to pressure-test the global financial system, with EM currencies and French government bonds under pressure.
geopolitical: War with Iran: support has wavered, and the election outcome shapes how hard Trump pushes militarily and economically against Iran.
Possible escalation of military action in the Middle East could disrupt energy markets and raise prices.
Russia-Ukraine: a Republican hold raises the risk of a forced deal to the disadvantage of Ukraine and Europe, while Democrats would press Trump to be tougher on Russia and support Ukraine.
US-China trade truce set to expire in January, with Taiwan arms sales, tariffs and trade/investment restrictions as potential trigger points.
Europe's shift toward more protectionist trade policies could bring new global trade tensions.

tension_points.bull_case: Polls and prediction markets point to a Democrat takeover, which would constrain Trump's legislative agenda and may ease inflation concerns, letting front-end yields drift lower in a split Congress.
tension_points.bear_case: A surprise Republican hold would push the 10yr above 5.5% and the 2yr to around 5% on fiscal worries and rate hike risk, and a Democrat win still leaves fiscal deficits and a possible shutdown over the debt ceiling.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Republican retention of both House and Senate on 3 November would invalidate the market's central Democrat-takeover discount.
